say: A caravan bound for a Shek town never arrived. The Guild keeps its word. Carry the factor four iron plates, then deal with whoever took the rest.
We lost a wagon train on the Shek road. The buyer wants his goods and the Guild wants its name kept clean. Four iron plates will do for now.
Contracts don't forgive delays. A shipment never reached a Shek shop. Bring him iron plates in its place, and find the man who ended the wagons.
Elric Vosk was hired to guard that caravan. It never arrived and the guards never returned. The shopkeeper still waits. Carry him iron, then find Vosk.
A broken delivery is a broken Guild. Take four iron plates to the Shek shopkeeper who was owed. Then see to the guard who vanished with the rest.
accepted: Bring four iron plates to a Shek shopkeeper. He will know the delivery. Then see to Elric Vosk and come back to me.
Shek shopkeeper, four iron plates. After that, the Guild wants Vosk. We pay on proof.
The shopkeeper is expecting someone. Give him the plates and tell him the Guild kept its word. Then Vosk.
Iron to the Shek town. Steel to Vosk. Report back when the second is done.

say: The Guild's wagons did not come. I have waited a month. You carry iron? Then the Guild still remembers its word.
Four plates. That isn't what was promised, but it's something. The wagons are lost, I think. I won't blame the Guild for the road.
Iron. Good. The wagons were late, then very late, then forgotten. At least someone remembers the debt.
A stranger with iron plates and a Guild stamp. I didn't expect it.
reply: That is all I could carry.
after: The guard who vanished with the cargo was called Elric Vosk. Tell the Guild I want him found, or at least buried.
Vosk was hired to watch the wagons. Now I hear he watches nothing. Find him.
Tell your Guild the iron is received. The rest is in Vosk's pocket. Take it back.
The Guild writes things down. If you do this well, they will write your name.

say: Vosk is dead? Then the wagons are paid for, one way or another. The Guild thanks you. Here are the cats.
A broken delivery repaid in blood. The Guild approves.
You carried iron and ended a thief. That's a good week's work. Here's the Guild's pay.
The caravan is a loss, but the man is gone. The shopkeeper sends his thanks. We send cats.
The nightmares never go away. There is a Meat Lord out in the plains. I will not send you without proof you can kill one of them.
You want a hunt? Bring me an arm. A painted one. I don't tell the nest to anyone who hasn't bled one.
I keep a list. Meat Lord is at the top. If you want to cross his name off, bring me proof you can end one of his.
The Meat Lord eats well and wastes nothing. I'd see him end. First a limb of the tribe, so I know you aren't a talker.
Plenty come asking for the hunt. Few return with a painted arm. Return with one, and I'll point you at the Lord.
accepted: A severed arm from the painted ones. Right hand will do. Bring it to a hunter, any hunter. Then the Meat Lord.
Take an arm from any cannibal you cut down. Bring it to us. We will tell you where the Lord eats.
The proof is a right arm. Do not waste it. A hunter will know what to do with it.
Kill one of them, take the arm, show it to a hunter. Then the Lord.

say: A painted arm. Good. You aren't a talker. The Meat Lord keeps his own table, past the edge of what we patrol.
That's a cannibal's arm. You have bled one, then. The Meat Lord eats where the plains turn red. You'll know it by the smell.
Proof enough. The Lord hunts in the plains and his men carry what he leaves. You'll find the camp by following the bones.
You killed one and kept the arm. That's more than most hunters manage. Listen carefully, for I say this once.
after: He is where the cannibals gather most thickly. Follow the bone fences and the smoke.
Do not go alone. Do not go slowly. Do not go hungry.
He will not run. He will feed. That is the only thing he knows.
I have a list of names. His is the only one I read aloud.

say: The Meat Lord is dead. The nightmares won't end, but they've lost a teller.
You ended the one at the top of my list. Here's what the hunters owe.
A painted arm and a dead Lord. You're the first to finish the hunt.
He's gone. The plains are quieter. Don't be fooled. Take the pay.
The University wants Rhinobot's CPU. Rhinobot wanted to help and had no moral processing. We would like to study what's left of him.
Finch is after a core. Not any core: Rhinobot's. Hear him first, then do the dirty part.
A robot with a conscience and no morals. The Machinists will pay for what's inside it. Go and see Finch about the details.
Ruins are our trade, and Rhinobot is a ruin that still walks. Talk to Finch, then bring his CPU to Iyo.
The scholars want a relic and the hunters want the pay. Finch will explain.
accepted: Finch will tell you what he needs. Bring Rhinobot's CPU to his assistant Iyo. Iyo handles the pay.
See Finch first. He knows the machine. Then bring the CPU to Iyo.
A relic is only worth what the scholars say. Finch says. Iyo pays.
Talk, kill, deliver. In that order. Do not mix them up.

say: You come from the hunters? Good. I need Rhinobot's CPU. He was a helpful machine with no capacity for harm assessment. I'd like to know why.
A CPU, from a machine called Rhinobot. It's an old design, and a flawed one. The flaw is of scholarly interest. The robot is of less.
Rhinobot wanted to help, and so he helped with anything. I should like the core intact. Bring it to my assistant.
Another hunter. Splendid. A core of ancient manufacture, from a robot who couldn't say no. Bring it to Iyo.
reply: I will bring it to Iyo.
after: Iyo will pay and note the delivery. Do not damage the core. I mean it.
He may attack on sight. He may help you. The line between is thin.
Careful with it. It remembers things.
The CPU has a chance of surviving a clean kill. Do not use fire.

say: Rhinobot's core. Intact. Finch will be insufferable. The University pays.
That's the CPU. I'll file it. You'll be paid. The Tech Hunters speak well of you.
A relic delivered. The Machinists are grateful.
You brought the core. Good. Payment is made. Don't touch the rest.
An ex-Anti-Slaver is bleeding our wagons. Pyke Ludlow. We pay for his end. First the pens need dressings: two medical supplies to the slave shop.
Ludlow has killed more of our guards than disease has. Take two medical supplies to the trader at the pens, then deal with the man.
Our guards come back cut. Our wagons don't come back. Pyke Ludlow is the reason. Carry dressings to the slave shop, then end him.
A rogue Anti-Slaver costs us more than the real ones. Dressings to the shop first, so the wounded can work. Then Ludlow.
Business is business. Ludlow kills our people and we pay for his death. Medical supplies to the slave shop, then Ludlow.
decline: I do not work for slavers.
accepted: Two medical supplies to a slave shop trader. Then Pyke Ludlow. Come back when he is dead.
Dressings to the pens, then the hunt. We pay on proof.
The trader at the shop will take your supplies and tell you what he knows. Then Ludlow.
Carry first, kill second, collect third.

say: Medical supplies. Finally. The guards have been coming back cut, and I've had nothing to bind them with.
Dressings for the wounded. Good. Ludlow strikes at the wagons and our men bleed on the road.
Two sets. They'll do for now. Pyke Ludlow hits where we least expect.
You carry supplies and a contract. Good. The man you want is Pyke Ludlow, and he isn't far from the roads.
after: He works the roads between the markets. He knows the wagons before they leave.
He was an Anti-Slaver once. The worst kind: a convert.
Find him and finish it. We have lost enough guards for the month.
We pay on proof, not on promise. Remember that.

say: Ludlow is dead. The wagons will travel in peace for a month.
You ended the rogue. The Slave Traders don't forget a favour.
A bad week ends well. Ludlow is gone. Here's what we promised.
Business concluded. Take the coin and don't ask where it came from.
A Guild caravan went out toward the Shek towns and never arrived. The guard's name was Vosk, I think.
Wagons don't vanish. People take them. The Guild is quiet about it, which means it's angry.
There's a shopkeeper in the east still waiting on a delivery.
Guild contracts go one of two ways. The goods arrive, or someone pays. Right now it's someone.
The Guild promised my cousin iron plates. They never came. The shopkeeper has stopped asking.
A merchant at the gate said his wagons are overdue. He did not look angry. He looked like a man making a list.
Foreign guards watching foreign wagons. When it goes wrong, it goes wrong in our dust.
Whoever took that caravan, the Guild will find. They keep better books than we do.
Elric Vosk took a job guarding a caravan and walked off with it. I heard that on the road.
The Mercenary Guild hasn't said a word about Vosk. That's the loudest thing I've heard all week.
Merchants are nervous. A caravan guard turned thief makes every guard a suspect.
A guard who kills the master and keeps the bell. That isn't mercenary work. That's something else.
Vosk is dead. The Guild paid for it, I heard. Caravans are still nervous but the guards are less so.
The man who took the wagons is gone. The goods aren't found. The Guild writes it off and moves on.
A shopkeeper in the east got his iron after all. That's the Guild for you: slow, but they pay.
Elric Vosk finally paid his debts.
That guard who took the caravan, Vosk, is dead. The Guild has stopped complaining about it.
Somebody finally put down Elric Vosk. The roads are a little safer for hired guards.
A thief with a sword and a bell. Gone. Nobody will miss the bell.
A guard who turned thief is dead. Merchants will sleep a little easier, and hire a little warier.
The hunters keep a list. The Meat Lord is at the top. Nobody has crossed him off yet.
Painted arms. That's how a hunter proves himself. A left one is for show. A right one is proof.
The nightmares never go away. We keep killing but they never go away.
Meat Lord eats well. The hunters don't.
The Meat Lord is somewhere out in the plains. The hunters want him dead. The rest of us want to stay far away.
Cannibal Hunters ask for painted arms as proof. I'd rather not know what they do with them.
I met a hunter once who said the Meat Lord eats his own kind when there's nothing else. I believe him.
Don't take the cannibal road without a hunter's blessing. The plains don't forgive.
The Meat Lord is dead. The hunters crossed him off the list and cut a notch in their belts.
A stranger brought a painted arm, and then a dead Lord. The hunters shake their heads and nod.
The plains are quieter. Don't be fooled. A new Lord is always hungry.
Word is, the hunters wept. I don't believe it. But I believe they stopped for a moment.
The Meat Lord is dead. The cannibals of the plains have lost a leader. They will have another by spring.
Somebody finally ended the big cannibal. The hunters paid.
The painted tribe is angrier now. Be careful on the plains road.
A Meat Lord is down and the plains aren't safer. The hunters say that's how it always goes.
Finch wants a CPU. Rhinobot's, specifically. The hunters are drawing lots.
Rhinobot wanted to help. That's the problem. A robot that helps with anything is dangerous.
The University pays for relics, not blood.
Iyo pays on delivery. Finch pays in lectures.
Machinists are after a robot's brain. It's a nice change from their usual books.
There's a bounty on a robot called Rhinobot. A robot, can you imagine.
Tech Hunters go into ruins and don't return. Rhinobot is a ruin that walks.
Mind the Ashlands. Old machines don't care who you are.
Rhinobot is down. The University got its core. I heard Finch cried. I don't believe it.
A robot that wanted to help is a pile of scrap. A stranger did it, for the Machinists.
Iyo paid in full. First time anyone has seen that.
The ruins are quiet. The scholars are loud.
People say a robot in the Ashlands is finished. The Machinists took its brain.
Rhinobot, the helpful one, is gone. I didn't know he was real.
Somebody has been dismantling the old machines. Somebody is getting paid for it.
The Machinists got their robot brain. I hope it was worth whatever they paid.
Pyke Ludlow hits the wagons and leaves the slaves loose. The Slave Traders want him found.
An Anti-Slaver turned killer. Even his own side doesn't like what he has become.
Guards come back cut and refuse to say who by. They say it anyway after a drink.
Ludlow has made more enemies than the whole of the Anti-Slavers.
Pyke Ludlow was one of us. Now he kills anyone who ever owned a chain. That isn't what we're for.
Ludlow is a stain on the cause. We would like him ended, but not by us.
A good man gone wrong. That's the worst kind.
The Anti-Slavers don't claim Ludlow. The Slave Traders have a price on his head. The two facts are related.
Pyke Ludlow is dead. The slavers say it was business. The Anti-Slavers say nothing.
A rogue Anti-Slaver ended. The wagons travel unguarded and nobody is happy about it.
Ludlow's gone. The Slave Traders paid someone. That someone isn't welcome in the pens.
The man who killed slavers and slaves alike has stopped. Few will say they miss him.
Pyke Ludlow is dead. The slaver wagons are moving again. That is the world.
Somebody killed Ludlow, the rogue. The Slave Traders paid. That sounds right and wrong at once.
A killer on the slave roads is down. The roads aren't safer, just quieter.
A killer who hunted the slave wagons is dead. Both sides pretend it was an accident.
A Shek shopkeeper told me he's still waiting on iron. Four plates, he said. Four plates is a thing to wait for.
The Guild is quiet when it loses a wagon. It is loud when it loses face. Right now it is loud.
I buy iron from the Guild. The price went up this month. They say it is the road. I think it is the thief.
Merchants lose caravans every year. It isn't the loss they remember. It's who took it.
A guard turned thief is the worst kind. He knows the route, the guards and the bell.
Vosk was a good hire once. That's how it starts.
I wouldn't take a caravan job this month. Not with Vosk loose on the road.
Caravan guards talk about Vosk the way a doctor talks about a disease that only attacks doctors.
A hunter won't tell you where the Meat Lord eats until you show him a painted arm. Bring a right one.
I sold a painted arm to a hunter once. He paid in dried meat and said it was a fair price. I did not ask what he did with it.
The Cannibal Hunters judge you by what you carry, not what you say.
Fresh arms keep poorly. Come back quickly.
Cannibals don't waste anything. A Meat Lord wastes less than the rest.
Painted ones leave bone fences around their camps. If you see a fence, turn around. If you see two, run.
The plains are quiet at night. That's when the hunters go in.
Nobody walks the plains for pleasure. Nobody walks them twice without a reason.
Iyo is the University's face to outsiders. He's polite, flat and very precise about what he pays for.
Finch doesn't leave the University. Iyo does the talking. Between them they decide what the world is worth.
Machinists pay late, but they pay. Tech Hunters bring them what the ruins give up.
The Tech Hunters' notes are free. The University's pay isn't.
Old machines still walk some ruins. They are not hostile. They are not friendly either. They simply do not understand you.
A robot that helps with anything is the most dangerous kind. It will help you into a grave.
Ruins keep their dead, and sometimes the dead keep their duties.
Hunters say the old machines remember. Remember what, no one will say.
Slave wagons have been getting hit on the open road. Guards come back cut and the wagons come back empty.
A man called Ludlow used to free slaves. Now he kills everyone near them. Slavers don't understand it.
The Slave Traders are paying extra for wagon guards. It doesn't help. The guards just die for more.
If you hear an Anti-Slaver talk about Ludlow, they do not use his name. They spit instead.
Shop trader here's short of bandages. The guards are coming back cut. He doesn't say by whom, but we all know.
The pens are quiet. When the pens are quiet, it means the guards are afraid.
Medical supplies cost more this month. The Slave Traders are buying all they can find.
A trader told me Ludlow knows our wagon routes.
